videos.caption: 9 Best Things to Do in Marrakesh 🕌✨ 1) Stay in a Riad 🛏️  feel the authentic Moroccan vibe, from the mosaic tiles to the whisper-quiet courtyards. Riads offer privacy, fewer crowds, and a home-away-from-home feel with traditional decor, often a peaceful rooftop terrace, and staff who treat you like family. Perfect for a truly Moroccan experience without the hotel hustle. 2) Best Coffee at Bacha Coffee ☕️✨ (Location: https://goo.gl/maps/6u3Xx9J9xqv1w9Qw7) Silky espresso, perfectly balanced blends, and a chic, relaxed atmosphere. Great latte art, friendly baristas, and a bright, stylish space to post your vibes. Pro tip: try their signature crush coffee and pastry pairing. 3) Explore the Souks 🧿🌀 Fun tip: haggle with a smile, never agree to the first price! Make it a playful game, sample spices, and test your bargaining skills. Lose yourself in ribbons of color, leather, pottery, and lamps. The thrill of the find is half the fun! 4) Visit Ben Youssef Madrasa 🕌 A jaw-dropping historic site with intricate tilework, carved wood, and serene courtyards. It’s a perfect spot for photos that scream old-world Marrakech charm. 5) Jardin Majorelle 🌿💙 iconic cobalt-blue paths, lush botanical displays, and a peaceful escape from the market buzz. A must-see for color lovers and plant enthusiasts, plus it’s connected to the Yves Saint Laurent legacy. 6) Ourika Valley Day Trip 🚙🌄 about 1 hour from central Marrakech (depending on traffic). What to expect: stunning valley scenery, Berber villages, waterfalls, and a cooler climate. A refreshing break from the medina with photo-worthy viewpoints. 7) Agafay Desert Experience 🐫🏜️ Highlights: camel ride under the open sky, squad  bike moments, and magical desert views. Luxe touch: stay at a desert camp with plush lounges, gourmet meals, and starlit dinners. Perfect for a memorable  outing. 8) Dinner at La Trattoria 🍝🇮🇹  warm, cozy ambiance with authentic Italian flavors in Marrakech. Great for a relaxed evening, fresh pastas, and a lively dining vibe after a day of exploration. 9) Jemaa el-Fnaa - The Heart of Marrakech 🎭💃 Do it for the vibes: bustling square, street performances, snake charmers, and a feast for the senses. Pro tip: bring some cash for photos with performers and for quick bites. Best times: late afternoon into evening when the energy peaks. #Marrakesh #Morocco #TravelTikTok #Riads #Souks

😍Morocco like Pinterest: the most beautiful hotels  🇲🇦  📍 Royal Mansour Marrakech One of the most luxurious hotels in the world, where every guest stays in a private riad with its own courtyard and pool. Carved ceilings, mosaics, and palm gardens. Breakfasts on the terrace and a spa under a glass dome. 📍 El Fenn A place where Morocco meets contemporary art. Bright walls, terracotta rooftop pools, vintage furniture, and rich colors. A bohemian vibe with sunsets overlooking the medina. 📍 La Mamounia A true Marrakech legend. Expansive gardens, arched galleries, emerald tiles, and a pool you’ll want to spend all day in. Classic luxury with history. 📍 Riad Yasmine The iconic Instagram riad with an emerald pool and pink walls. Small, cozy, and incredibly photogenic. Breakfast by the pool with flower petals. 📍 Amanjena Minimalism with Moroccan architecture. Sandy tones, reflective pools, and perfect symmetry. 📍 Kasbah Tamadot A hotel in the Atlas Mountains with views over the valleys. Terraces, Berber style, and warm sunset light. 📍 The Oberoi Marrakech Modern luxury with an oriental touch. Grand pools, arches, reflective water, and clean geometry. 📍 Scarabeo Camp White tents in the Agafay desert. Minimalism, sand dunes, camels, and caramel-colored sunsets. #moroccotravel #luxuryhotels #riadlife #travelinspo #bucketlist

Between 1921 and 1927, #Spanish colonial forces dropped tons of toxic mustard gas across Rif (Northern #morocco ) They deliberately targeted my tribe (Riffians)  and agricultural land.  Northern Morocco still accounts for anoverwhelmingly high percentage of the country’s cancer cases, forcing families to carry the heavy weight of a war that ended a century ago. Historical crimes don’t just stay trapped inside history books. They live on in our bodies, our health, and our daily reality. We remember the past not only to honor those who survived, but to demand recognition for everything that was lost. #amazigh#European#WW1

Would you wander Marrakech alone?  One thing I was honestly nervous about before coming to Marrakech for the first time was safety, especially as a woman travelling alone. Social media can make the medina look super intimidating, chaotic, and overwhelming, but my experience has actually been really positive. Of course you need to stay aware like in any big city, but I’ve spent hours wandering the souks, getting lost in little alleyways, shopping, stopping for mint tea, and exploring on my own and I genuinely felt okay. One thing that helped SO much this time was not carrying all my luggage around with me 😅 dragging a huge backpack through crowded streets instantly makes you feel more stressed and overwhelmed. I used @bounce luggage storage so I could explore Marrakech freely for the day before my riad check-in, and it made such a difference. I could actually enjoy the medina instead of worrying about my bags the entire time. Bounce has thousands of locations worldwide and is a super reliable resource if you find yourself in a similar situation as me. If you’re travelling soon, you can use my code SARAHBOUNCE for a discount! #travelhacks #travelreccommendations #solotraveller
